# Code of Conduct

## Our standard

Carry One contributors, collaborators, testers, and community members should help keep the project respectful, safe, and focused on constructive work.

Expected behavior includes:

- communicating with respect and good faith;
- giving specific, actionable feedback;
- respecting privacy and consent;
- avoiding harassment, discrimination, intimidation, or personal attacks;
- never pressuring someone to participate in a mission, wallet transaction, test, or public demonstration;
- treating security disclosures and private participant information carefully.

## Unacceptable behavior

Unacceptable behavior includes harassment, threats, doxxing, discriminatory conduct, deliberate disruption, deceptive/scam-like activity, misuse of private wallet/user information, or attempts to use Carry One for illegal, exploitative, wagering, or non-consensual activity.

## Project-specific consent rule

Carry One's product law is explicit: **No one becomes a bridge by surprise.** The same principle applies to project participation. Testers and destinations must knowingly consent to their role, and no one should be represented publicly without permission.

## Enforcement

If you experience or observe unacceptable behavior, contact the repository owner privately through the existing team communication channel. Reports will be reviewed in context and may result in warnings, removal from project spaces, revocation of access, or other proportionate action.

## Scope

This code applies in repository collaboration, demos, test sessions, community discussions, and other spaces where someone is representing Carry One.
